dev.to:4820042: Builds a crash-safe, schedulable PostgreSQL workflow with pg_durable and pg_duckdb to archive cold rows as Parquet in Azure Blob, checkpointing export, validation, deletion, and audit steps so interrupted runs resume safely.
dev.to:4819672: Demonstrates archiving 2021 rows from a 10-million-row PostgreSQL sales table to Parquet in Azure Blob with pg_duckdb, deleting them from the live table, and continuing to query and aggregate live and archived data together through read_parquet().
dev.to:4814378: Runs pg_duckdb against a 10-million-row PostgreSQL sales table on Azure Flexible Server, showing benefits for heavy grouping but not simple aggregates, with DuckDBScan plans, query-scoped forcing, and numeric precision compatibility caveats.
dev.to:4812637: Installs the full open-source pg_duckdb extension on Azure Database for PostgreSQL to read and write Azure Blob Parquet and accelerate local tables, contrasting its accessible DuckDB engine with Aurora Analytics' sealed, read-only foreign-data wrapper.
dev.to:4803170: Reproduces the same Parquet query in Aurora Analytics and open-source pg_duckdb, using matching plans to establish DuckDB underneath while showing Aurora exposes only a read-only foreign-data wrapper and pg_duckdb offers direct DuckDB SQL, local-table acceleration, and lake writes.
dev.to:4788485: Compares keyset pagination across PostgreSQL, YugabyteDB, MySQL, MongoDB, Oracle, and SQL Server, showing how correctly typed row comparisons form composite index bounds while OR expansions and datatype mismatches can degrade to wider scans and filters.
dev.to:4797344: Traces Oracle FETCH FIRST from a ROW_NUMBER() analytic rewrite in 12c to the ROWNUM and COUNT STOPKEY rewrite in current 23ai and 26ai, compares PostgreSQL's native Limit node, and explains why execution plans determine whether Top-N queries stop early.
dev.to:4722887: Benchmarks DocumentDB 0.117 scalar $group index pushdown on 50,000 documents, replacing full-document reads with a covered index-only scan using 24 buffer hits and no heap fetches, while MongoDB 8 requires a hint to choose its covered index path.
dev.to:4745326: Shows DocumentDB 0.109 using one Extended RUM compound multikey index to cover $match, descending $sort, $limit, and $project without a separate filter or sort, reproducing MongoDB-style one-to-many document access on PostgreSQL.
dev.to:4722896: Benchmarks DocumentDB 0.116 prefix sort pushdown for $sort followed by $group, streaming 50,000 ordered index entries instead of the blocking hash or 14 MB disk-spilling sort in 0.114; the 0.117 distinct-scan option reduces the work to 100 keys and documents.
